<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914293_theRebbe_757" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914293_theRebbe_757__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header of the maamar, including the date and the yahrtzeit of the Rebbe Maharash.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">On the eve of the thirteenth of Tishrei,</t>
    <t s="2">the yahrtzeit of the Rebbe Maharash,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5740.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section introduces the verse about dwelling in sukkos and discusses the necessity of knowledge as part of the mitzvah, the paradox of settlement within a surrounding light, and the unique unity of all Israel in the sukkah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"You shall dwell in sukkos for seven days; every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos."</t>
    <t s="1">(And the reason for this is)</t>
    <t s="2">"So that your generations may know that I caused the children of Israel to dwell in sukkos when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, etc."</t>
    <t s="3">And from the language of the verse</t>
    <t s="4">("so that your generations may know, etc.")</t>
    <t s="5">we learn</t>
    <t s="6">that this knowledge is</t>
    <t s="7">(not only a matter of the intention of the mitzvah,</t>
    <t s="8">but rather)</t>
    <t s="9">a part of the fulfillment of the mitzvah</t>
    <t s="10">(as is also evident from the language of the Alter Rebbe in his Shulchan Aruch).</t>
    <t s="11">And the precise points of our Nesi'im regarding this are known:</t>
    <t s="12">Why is this knowledge so crucial</t>
    <t s="13">that it is a part of the mitzvah?</t>
    <t s="14">And also, what is the meaning of "You shall dwell in sukkos"?</t>
    <t s="15">For a sukkah is a level of encompassing light (makif), and the matter of settlement</t>
    <t s="16">(for "teishvu" also includes the interpretation of settlement)</t>
    <t s="17">specifically relates to a level of internal light (pnimi),</t>
    <t s="18">and from the fact that it says "You shall dwell in sukkos," it proves that even after the dwelling, it remains a level of encompassing light,</t>
    <t s="19">and the matter of settlement must be within the encompassing light.</t>
    <t s="20">Also, one must understand what is written: "Every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos,"</t>
    <t s="21">for the command "You shall dwell in sukkos" is for all of Israel; what does "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos" add?</t>
    <t s="22">And in the command "You shall dwell in sukkos," it says "seven days," whereas in the command "every native-born, etc.," it says "shall dwell in sukkos" without specification.</t>
    <t s="23">And behold, from this verse</t>
    <t s="24">("every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos")</t>
    <t s="25">we learn</t>
    <t s="26">that all of Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah.</t>
    <t s="27">And it must be said:</t>
    <t s="28">Behold, the matter of the unity of all of Israel</t>
    <t s="29">(the matter of "You are standing today, all of you")</t>
    <t s="30">exists also throughout the entire year,</t>
    <t s="31">to the extent that the mitzvah of loving a fellow Jew</t>
    <t s="32">[the reason for which is that they are all compatible and have one Father for all of them</t>
    <t s="33">(the matter of unity)</t>
    <t s="34">as explained in Tanya]</t>
    <t s="35">is the entire Torah, and the rest is its explanation,</t>
    <t s="36">meaning that every mitzvah is like an explanation and detail of the matter of the unity of all of Israel,</t>
    <t s="37">so why is this specifically emphasized in the mitzvah of sukkah?</t>
    <t s="38">And also, one must understand what is written</t>
    <t s="39">(before this)</t>
    <t s="40">"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, a branch of a thick-leaved tree, and willows of the brook,"</t>
    <t s="41">and it is known</t>
    <t s="42">that this mitzvah has a connection to the matter of the sukkah,</t>
    <t s="43">which is why the preferred mitzvah is that the taking of the Four Species should be in the sukkah.</t>
    <t s="44">For this is also the connection of the taking of the Four Species to the level of Daas (knowledge),</t>
    <t s="45">(similar to "so that they may know" regarding the sukkah),</t>
    <t s="46">as it is stated in the writings of the Arizal</t>
    <t s="47">that the intent of the waving of the lulav is to draw down Daas to the Nukva of Zeir Anpin, which stands at the chest of Zeir Anpin</t>
    <t s="48">(which is why the lulav and its species must touch the chest).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the general service of drawing down the encompassing light into settlement, paralleling the progression from faith to comprehension throughout one's life and even in Moshe Rabbeinu's level.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing the matter of drawing down the encompassing light with settlement</t>
    <t s="2">("You shall dwell in sukkos")</t>
    <t s="3">in the service of G-d as it is throughout the life of a person in general,</t>
    <t s="4">and likewise in every single day.</t>
    <t s="5">For although this matter in its essence is during the festival of Sukkos,</t>
    <t s="6">"You shall dwell in sukkos,"</t>
    <t s="7">nevertheless, the Torah was stated in generalities and specifics,</t>
    <t s="8">and there is a semblance of this matter also throughout the entire year.</t>
    <t s="9">And the explanation is:</t>
    <t s="10">Behold, the two matters of encompassing light (makif) and internal light (pnimi) in the service of G-d in general are faith and comprehension.</t>
    <t s="11">And first, the matter of the encompassing light of the sukkah must be explained,</t>
    <t s="12">and afterwards, "You shall dwell in sukkos" must be explained,</t>
    <t s="13">for the beginning of service is in the level of faith.</t>
    <t s="14">For every single Jew,</t>
    <t s="15">as soon as he comes into the world,</t>
    <t s="16">has within him a level of faith,</t>
    <t s="17">as our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="18">"Israel are believers, children of believers."</t>
    <t s="19">For this is a true description, according to the Torah of truth, of every single Jew.</t>
    <t s="20">And after he reaches the age of education, etc., and comes to possess Daas (intellect),</t>
    <t s="21">behold, what was initially for him in the level of faith and encompassing light</t>
    <t s="22">is drawn into a level of internalization and settlement,</t>
    <t s="23">to the extent that this becomes his entire existence.</t>
    <t s="24">Nevertheless, even then he has a level of faith,</t>
    <t s="25">for after and through the drawing down of the encompassing light</t>
    <t s="26">(what was previously in the level of encompassing light)</t>
    <t s="27">into internalization,</t>
    <t s="28">a higher level of encompassing light is drawn down,</t>
    <t s="29">and this encompassing light is in the level of faith.</t>
    <t s="30">And likewise, throughout all the days of his life,</t>
    <t s="31">the more he elevates himself in his service and in his comprehension,</t>
    <t s="32">what was initially for him in the level of faith</t>
    <t s="33">is drawn into understanding and comprehension,</t>
    <t s="34">and his faith is in a more elevated level</t>
    <t s="35">[and similar to the general collective of the children of Israel,</t>
    <t s="36">that initially they were included among the nations of the world,</t>
    <t s="37">whose faith is only in the level of the power of the actor within the acted-upon,</t>
    <t s="38">and afterwards they were elevated, etc., so that their faith was in the level of the One who transcends the world,</t>
    <t s="39">as explained in the Siddur, Shaar HaChag HaMatzos, at its beginning].</t>
    <t s="40">To the extent that our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="41">"Believe in every matter of Moshe Rabbeinu,"</t>
    <t s="42">even though Moshe was the ultimate perfection of wisdom,</t>
    <t s="43">behold, even after the perfection of comprehension, there are matters that are in the level of faith, beyond comprehension.</t>
    <t s="44">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="45">the more one comprehends, the comprehension itself necessitates that there are matters that are beyond intellect,</t>
    <t s="46">to the extent of the statement,</t>
    <t s="47">"The ultimate knowledge is that we do not know You."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
